incidents.title: Deepfake videos of PM Lee and DPM Wong promote crypto and investment scams
incidents.summary: Fake videos using the likeness of Prime Minister Lee Hsien Loong, and separately Deputy PM Lawrence Wong, were used to promote cryptocurrency and investment schemes. The date is PM Lee's public warning, the earliest public record found; the videos had been circulating for some days.

incidents.title: Second deepfake of Lee Hsien Loong promotes an investment product
incidents.summary: A new deepfake showed Lee Hsien Loong, by then Senior Minister, endorsing an investment product with guaranteed returns. He warned the public again.
incidents.notes: Exact day not confirmed from a primary source.

incidents.title: Deepfake videos and voice clones of PM Lawrence Wong promote scams
incidents.summary: AI-generated video and a cloned voice of Prime Minister Wong were used to promote cryptocurrency, money-making schemes and PR services.

incidents.title: Grok image-tool misuse (sexualised deepfakes): Singapore exposure
incidents.summary: From late December 2025 the Grok chatbot on X was widely used to produce non-consensual sexualised edits of real people. The sources checked do not quantify local complaints in Singapore. The case is included because the service was available and the regulator engaged X.
incidents.notes: Onset date is the start of a documented analysis window of mass misuse; sources vary on the exact start. Local harm not quantified.

incidents.title: Grok image-tool misuse (sexualised deepfakes): Indonesia
incidents.summary: Reports that Grok produced sexualised images of real women and minors led Indonesia's communications ministry to begin investigating in early January 2026.
incidents.source_title: Marketing-Interactive on IMDA and regional action
incidents.notes: Same onset rule as the other Grok cases.

incidents.title: Deepfakes of President Prabowo and Finance Minister Sri Mulyani used in fake aid scams
incidents.summary: Fraudsters used AI-generated videos of senior officials to promise cash aid and collect fees through WhatsApp. One suspect reportedly took about Rp65 million from around 100 victims from December 2024. The OECD incident monitor records a related scam across 20 provinces.
incidents.notes: Onset is 'since December 2024' per the source, so lags are approximate.

incidents.title: Deepfake of Finance Minister Sri Mulyani calling teachers a 'burden'
incidents.summary: A manipulated clip cut from her 7 August 2025 speech falsely showed the minister calling teachers a burden on the state. An official later said false content had fuelled anger and protests; that causal link is the official's claim and is not independently established here.
incidents.notes: Date is the minister's own denial, the earliest public record found.

incidents.title: Deepfake news-anchor and PM videos promote investment schemes on Facebook
incidents.summary: AI-manipulated videos imitating Bernama TV news anchors, and a fake clip of PM Anwar Ibrahim, promoted dubious investment schemes on Facebook after repeated incidents. Earlier circulation is likely, so this is a running series and not a single dated event.
incidents.notes: Onset unknown, so no response lag is computed for this series.

incidents.title: Grok image-tool misuse (sexualised deepfakes): Malaysia
incidents.summary: MCMC recorded 17 complaints or reports about Grok misuse in Malaysia: six formal complaints, two police reports, eight social-media tagging complaints and one First Information Report opened by MCMC. Content involved women and minors.

incidents.title: Deepfake audio of President Marcos 'ordering' military action
incidents.summary: Manipulated audio imitating President Marcos appeared to direct the armed forces to act against a foreign country, during South China Sea tensions and a joint military exercise. Officials said the clip was fake and probably produced by a foreign actor.
incidents.notes: Date is the first official statement, the earliest public record found.

incidents.title: Grok image-tool misuse (sexualised deepfakes): Philippines
incidents.summary: Authorities cited Grok's capacity to generate sexually explicit, non-consensual deepfake material, including content that could involve minors.

incidents.title: Deepfake video-call impersonation scams
incidents.summary: Scammers took over Zalo and Facebook accounts and used the owners' photos and videos to stage fake video calls asking contacts for money.
incidents.notes: Date is the earliest report found.

incidents.title: Deepfake sextortion of individuals and entrepreneurs
incidents.summary: Criminals used face-swapped explicit videos to extort victims, including a Hanoi schoolgirl in March 2024 and entrepreneurs in Ho Chi Minh City in early 2024.

incidents.title: Deepfake Zoom call impersonating PM Wong and other officials costs a victim at least S$4.9 million
incidents.summary: Scammers contacted a business professional on WhatsApp, posing as the Secretary to the Cabinet, and invited him to a fabricated Zoom meeting featuring AI-generated versions of the Prime Minister, the President and other officials. He transferred at least S$4.9 million before realising on 14 May 2026 that it was fake. The date is the Singapore Police Force advisory; the scam began earlier.
incidents.notes: Onset unknown (the money moved in several transfers before 14 May), so no response lag is computed. Also cited in TFGI's Perspectives series on AI readiness (10 Nov 2026).

incidents.title: Thai PM targeted by an AI voice-clone scam impersonating another leader
incidents.summary: Prime Minister Paetongtarn Shinawatra said she received a realistic voice message mimicking a well-known ASEAN leader, whom she did not name, asking for a donation and claiming Thailand was the only member yet to contribute. She said she nearly fell for it. The date is her public account; the call came earlier.
incidents.notes: The date of the call itself is not stated in the sources checked, so no response lag is computed.

incidents.title: AI face-altering video-call scam impersonating police, run from a Poipet call centre
incidents.summary: A call-centre gang operating from Poipet, Cambodia, impersonated Thai police on video calls and used AI to alter the callers' faces. Police said it targeted at least 163 people; one victim, a Thai-British beauty queen, lost 4 million baht. Thailand's Central Investigation Bureau arrested two suspects on 2 and 3 February 2025.
incidents.notes: The date is the arrests, the first public record, so the scam itself was earlier and undated. The Star reports the two suspects said they were forced to work for the gang.

incidents.title: AI-generated 'pilot' persona lures a 66-year-old woman to Chiang Mai airport
incidents.summary: A 66-year-old woman from Lampang travelled alone to Chiang Mai International Airport to meet a man she believed was a pilot, then learned he was an AI-generated character on Facebook. The OECD monitor classifies the harm as psychological; the sources listed do not report a financial loss.
incidents.source_title: OECD AI Incidents and Hazards Monitor, 17 Sep 2026
incidents.notes: Underlying Bangkok Post article (17 Sep 2026) read in full 22 Nov 2026: a 66-year-old woman from Lampang travelled to Chiang Mai airport on the evening of 16 Sep to meet a man she believed was a pilot; officers concluded his photo appeared AI-generated and posted on Facebook. No financial loss reported. No official response found.

incidents.title: Deepfake videos of JG Summit CEO Lance Gokongwei used to promote fake crypto and forex schemes
incidents.summary: The Securities and Exchange Commission warned that scammers were using deepfake video and audio of Lance Gokongwei, president and CEO of JG Summit Holdings, to endorse fraudulent crypto and forex investments. The date is the SEC warning, the earliest public record found.
incidents.source_title: AI Incident Database 1148 (reports on the SEC warning)
incidents.notes: Verified from the incident-database entry; the SEC advisory itself was not opened. Onset unknown.

incidents.title: AI-assisted romance scams using deepfake personas draw police and CICC alerts
incidents.summary: The Cybercrime Investigation and Coordinating Center (CICC) and the Philippine National Police issued alerts about AI-assisted romance scams, in which scammers use AI-generated personas. The civil-society group Scam Watch Pilipinas cited a retired school principal who lost 2.5 million pesos. This is a running series, not one dated event.
incidents.notes: Underlying articles read in full 22 Nov 2026: Philstar and PhilstarLife (both 4 Feb 2026) confirm the PNP Anti-Cybercrime Group and CICC warnings about AI-assisted love scams and deepfake personas; SecurityMatters (12 Feb 2026, citing PIA) confirms the Scam Watch Pilipinas case of a retired principal who lost ₱2.5 million. The PNP/CICC 'Red Alert' was issued 4 Feb 2026.

incidents.title: Deepfake Zoom call impersonating company executives costs a finance director over US$499,000
incidents.summary: A finance director of a multinational was contacted on WhatsApp on 24 Mar 2025 by a scammer posing as the CFO, then joined a Zoom call on 25 Mar in which the CEO and other executives were impersonated using deepfake technology. He transferred over US$499,000 (~S$670,000) on 26 Mar 2025; the scam was discovered on 27 Mar and Singapore/Hong Kong police withheld/seized the funds on 28 Mar.
incidents.notes: Date is first contact (24 Mar) per the SPF release of 7 Apr 2025, the earliest public record found; transfer 26 Mar, discovery 27 Mar, recovery 28 Mar. No OECD AIM entry found for this case; the OECD entry 2026-05-14-1081 is the different S$4.9m case (SG-I-05). SPF/MAS/CSA issued a joint advisory on 12 Mar 2025 warning of exactly this scam variant; it predates the incident, so it is recorded here, not as a response row.

incidents.title: Deepfake nude photos of students at a Singapore sports school created and shared by classmates
incidents.summary: Male students at a Singapore sports school generated and circulated deepfake nude images of female schoolmates from June 2024, using two WhatsApp groups (one to generate, one to circulate). The case became public on 12 Nov 2024. The school lodged a police report and disciplined students involved, including caning, suspension and sports-trip bans.
incidents.notes: Onset month from a victim's parent via CNA ('dates back to June'); exact start day unknown. No OECD AIM entry found for this case. Students aged 13-18. School not named in the tracker text: schools are not named in sexual-deepfake cases involving minors (the school name stays in the source link).

incidents.title: Deepfake sextortion emails target over 100 public servants including five ministers
incidents.summary: From 26 Nov 2024, more than 100 civil servants across 31 government agencies, including 12 political office-holders / five ministers, received extortion emails with fake compromising photos of themselves, demanding US$50,000 in cryptocurrency. No monetary loss was reported. MDDI confirmed the incident and police were investigating.
incidents.notes: MDDI statement as reported 29 Nov 2024; the primary MDDI statement itself was not opened.

incidents.title: Deepfake video of President Jokowi speaking Mandarin
incidents.summary: AI-manipulated video falsely showed President Joko Widodo delivering a speech in Mandarin (the original was a 2015 speech in English). It circulated in October 2023 ahead of the 2024 presidential election. Kominfo debunked it on 26 October 2023, explaining how the deepfake was produced. Date is the Kominfo debunk, the earliest verified public record found; the video circulated earlier in October.
incidents.source_title: Blackbird.AI: Deepfakes in the Indonesian election
incidents.notes: OECD AIM lists this as a hazard (2023-12-05-b2db). Kominfo debunk date 26 Oct 2023 from Verihubs and the DKPP journal bibliography; the CNN Indonesia page itself could not be opened.

incidents.title: AI-generated nude images of 300+ female students at a Seremban secondary school
incidents.summary: A Form Five student allegedly used AI to generate explicit deepfake images of female schoolmates, stored on his phone and circulated among students, allegedly sold via Telegram. Discovered 12 Aug 2026 when a Form Two student found the phone in the school surau; five police reports lodged 20-23 Aug 2026; school confirmed 300+ victims on 15 Sep 2026. Date is the first public reporting (The Star, 17 Oct 2026).
incidents.source_title: Media Selangor, 19 Oct 2026 (reporting Harian Metro; see also The Star, 17 Oct 2026)
incidents.notes: OECD AIM has two entries for this case (2026-10-15-dc0c and 2026-10-18-8df8); treat as one incident. Source switched 22 Nov 2026 from the AI Risk Wire aggregator (machine-generated, unverified) to Media Selangor (19 Oct 2026, reporting Harian Metro), which supports the 300+ victims, Telegram circulation/sale, 12 Aug discovery, five reports 20-23 Aug and 15 Sep confirmation; the victims' ages and the 'around 200 images' figure could not be verified against an accessible source and were removed.

incidents.title: 713 AI-generated deepfake posts targeting political leaders removed since January 2025
incidents.summary: Malaysian authorities removed 713 AI-generated deepfake social media posts targeting political leaders, following public complaints and legal violations. MCMC coordinated the takedowns. This is a running series from January 2025, not a single dated event; date is the OECD AIM entry date.
incidents.notes: Onset unknown, so no response lag. Overlaps thematically with MY-I-01 (investment-scam deepfakes of leaders) but is a distinct official count of political-leader deepfakes; kept separate.

incidents.title: Claude-powered commercial election-manipulation platform targeting Malaysian voters
incidents.summary: Anthropic's threat report (10 Sep 2026) disclosed case GTG-84005: an Istanbul-based firm, BBS Bilisim Teknolojileri, allegedly used Claude to build a commercial election-manipulation platform targeting Malaysian users — voter profiling across all 222 parliamentary constituencies using census/electoral data, ~1,000 fake X accounts, a fake news site (Malaysia Pulse) and a YouTube channel. Anthropic terminated the Claude accounts. The firm denied involvement. Anthropic found no evidence the campaign reached genuine online communities. Operation ran Dec 2025-Aug 2026 per the report.
incidents.source_title: Marketing-Interactive: MCMC presses Anthropic over alleged Malaysia election manipulation
incidents.notes: Date is the Anthropic report publication (10 Sep 2026); OECD AIM dates the incident 11 Sep 2026. The underlying Anthropic report was not opened; facts rest on secondary reporting of it.

incidents.title: Deepfake video impersonating Border Control Agency (AKPS) director-general
incidents.summary: AI-generated deepfake video falsely depicted the director-general of the Malaysian Border Control and Protection Agency (AKPS), aiming to damage his reputation and mislead the public. AKPS confirmed the video was fake, warned the public and announced potential legal action.
incidents.notes: AIM summary only; the underlying article was not opened. The second AIM entry (2025-12-07-ca89) is confirmed as a distinct incident — see MY-I-08 (two TikTok videos, 7 Dec 2025, false aid-support claims).

incidents.title: AI deepfake scam impersonating Johor state executive councillor on TikTok
incidents.summary: Multiple TikTok accounts used AI-generated images and voice to impersonate Johor state executive councillor Khairin-Nisa Ismail, promoting a fake aid scheme to steal personal data. Authorities shut down 12 accounts and are investigating.
incidents.notes: Response now recorded: MCMC took down the 12 accounts; announced by Johor police chief Datuk Ab Rahaman Arsad on 24 Feb 2026 — see MY-R-15. Police report lodged by Khairin-Nisa Ismail on 20 Feb 2026; some accounts active since 9 Feb 2026. Four of the 12 accounts used her face and voice via AI.

incidents.title: Philippine officials share Veo 3-generated video of fake students opposing Vice President Sara Duterte's impeachment
incidents.summary: A Veo 3-generated video styled as a street interview showed two AI-invented schoolboys opposing the impeachment of VP Sara Duterte. Posted on Facebook 14 Jun 2025, it was shared by Senator Ronald dela Rosa on 15 Jun and by Davao City Mayor Sebastian Duterte; it reached millions of views. The video depicts invented people, not a real person's likeness. A second Veo clip (an AI elderly fish-vendor arguing for impeachment) also circulated.
incidents.notes: Date is the original Facebook post (14 Jun); sharing by officials was 15 Jun. No OECD AIM entry found for this incident despite targeted searches; the 16 Jun 2025 backlog date appears to be the PCO response date.

incidents.title: AI deepfake video falsely shows Đồng Nai teacher crying over alleged sale of students' milk
incidents.summary: AI-generated deepfake videos falsely depicting a teacher crying after allegedly selling students' milk were widely shared on social media, causing public confusion and reputational harm. Police confirmed the videos were fabricated using AI.
incidents.notes: Date is the AIM listing date; confirm onset from the underlying article. Theme online-safety (synthetic-media misinformation/reputational harm) — no exact tracker theme fits; political-deepfakes was considered and rejected.

incidents.title: AI deepfake extortion scheme targets officials in Thanh Hóa
incidents.summary: In Thanh Hóa, nearly 20 individuals including government officials were targeted by extortionists using AI-assisted technology to create fake, sensitive images and videos; victims were threatened with public exposure unless large sums were paid, causing psychological distress and financial harm. (OECD AIM listing date; onset unconfirmed.)
incidents.notes: Date is the AIM listing date; onset unconfirmed — the underlying VietReader article (4 Oct 2026, read in full 22 Nov 2026) reports Thanh Hóa police disclosing on 4 Oct that they had received multiple reports from victims, with demands up to VND 1.5 billion, but gives no earlier dated record of when the extortion began. No police action beyond the warning is recorded.

incidents.title: AI deepfake extortion and fraud crackdown: cross-border rings targeting officials and businesspeople
incidents.summary: Vietnamese authorities disrupted criminal groups using AI-powered deepfake technology to fabricate sensitive images for extortion and fraud; investigations revealed cross-border networks involving Chinese nationals and local operatives targeting public officials and businesspeople through biometric spoofing, prompting coordinated raids across several provinces.
incidents.notes: Date is the AIM listing date; confirm onset from the underlying article. The crackdown itself is also the response — see VN-R-08.

incidents.title: Deepfake of Thai PBS World anchor and Miss Universe CEO promotes fake investment
incidents.summary: A purported AI deepfake impersonated Thai PBS World anchor Doliyana Bunnak interviewing Miss Universe Organization CEO Anne Jakkraphong Jakrajutatip, inviting investment from 8,000 baht with promised returns of hundreds of thousands. Thai PBS Verify found it fake; the underlying footage was from the 24 June 2025 Thai PBS World Tonight broadcast.
incidents.notes: Date is the original broadcast date per AIID; Thai PBS Verify publication date not confirmed in sources opened. No government/regulator response found.

incidents.title: Deepfake 'Crystallum AI' investment ad impersonates Thai PBS World anchors and business figures
incidents.summary: A Facebook ad misusing the Thai PBS World Tonight logo showed an anchor (former NHK World anchor Patchari Raksawong, who never anchored for Thai PBS) interviewing Central Group's Tos Chirathivat and Kalin Sarasin, promoting 'CRYSTALLUM AI' with a promised fivefold return. Thai PBS Verify traced the footage to a 2013 NHK flood report; HIVE Moderation gave a 72.3% probability of AI generation.
incidents.notes: Thai PBS Verify is a media fact-check, not a government response; Central Group's warning is corporate. No government/regulator response found.

incidents.title: AI sexual deepfakes of Semarang high-school students and teacher spread on X; maker later convicted
incidents.summary: AI-edited pornographic photos and videos using the faces of female students and at least one teacher of a Semarang high school spread on X from the account of an 18-year-old university student and alumnus: 300+ posts and 1,100 files stored. Victims included students, alumni and teaching staff.
incidents.notes: Onset is the 20 Oct 2025 Kompas report date, the earliest public record found; the posts began earlier in October. School not named in the tracker text: schools are not named in sexual-deepfake cases involving minors (the school name stays in the source link).

incidents.title: World App iris-scan biometric collection halted by privacy regulator
incidents.summary: Tools for Humanity's World App collected iris biometrics via Orb verification in the Philippines, incentivising scans with monetary rewards. The National Privacy Commission found the processing violated the Data Privacy Act and ordered it halted.
incidents.notes: Date is the cease-and-desist order, the earliest verified public record; the launch date was not verified, so onset_certainty is unknown.

incidents.title: Deepfake video of former president Halimah Yacob criticising the government circulates ahead of GE2025
incidents.summary: A deepfake video falsely showed former president Halimah Yacob making negative statements about the government, including a cloned voice. She said on 15 April 2025 she would file a police report.
incidents.notes: Whether the police report was actually filed is not confirmed. Halimah was not a candidate, so ELIONA's application to this clip is unclear.

incidents.title: Deepfake videos red-tag Makabayan bloc candidates as NPA recruiters during 2025 campaign
incidents.summary: Facebook pages posted AI deepfake videos depicting Makabayan candidates (including France Castro, Sarah Jane Elago, Teddy Casiño) as recruiters for the New People's Army, alongside manipulated audio. A 31 Jan video's audio scored 1/100 on a deepfake voice-detection tool. Castro appealed to COMELEC and DICT on 11 March 2025 to remove the videos.
incidents.notes: No specific COMELEC/DICT action on the 11 March appeal was found, so no response row is proposed. The general DICT-COMELEC Threat Monitoring Center is not tied to this complaint.

incidents.title: Deepfake romance-scam network fugitives arrested in Da Nang
incidents.summary: Three South Korean nationals who allegedly ran a Bavet-based romance-scam network using deepfakes to pose as women online were arrested in Da Nang after fleeing Cambodia on Interpol Red Notices. The network allegedly scammed about US$1 million between August and December 2024.
incidents.notes: Date is the arrest (28 Oct 2025); earliest public record is the police statement reported 5 Dec 2025. Scam activity itself was Aug-Dec 2024.

incidents.title: Deepfake ads impersonate Finance Minister Ekniti to promote investments
incidents.summary: AI-generated clips cloning the face and voice of Deputy PM and Finance Minister Ekniti Nitithanprapas circulated on Facebook and YouTube promoting investment schemes and loan apps falsely claiming Finance Ministry endorsement.
incidents.notes: Secondary sources citing Thaiger/Thairath/THE STANDARD; primary Thai reports not opened.

incidents.title: AI-generated video of Senate President Hun Sen falsely soliciting funds to wage war against Thailand
incidents.summary: Deepfake video repurposing footage of Hun Sen's 27 June meeting with civil servants in Preah Vihear, with a fabricated AI Thai voice track in which he purportedly asks viewers to transfer 300 baht via TrueMoney to fund a military force against Thailand, promising 50,000 baht in return.
incidents.notes: 27 June is the date AIID assigns and the date of the original Preah Vihear meeting whose footage was reused; AIID's own text says only that the video surfaced in late June 2025, so the exact circulation day is unconfirmed. Original news article behind Report 5442 (captioned 'MPTC condemns deepfake video of Senate President') could not be located despite targeted searches, so the MPTC statement's exact date is also unconfirmed.

incidents.title: AI-generated fake video imitating Prime Minister Hun Manet's voice
incidents.summary: Facebook account used AI to create a fake video imitating Prime Minister Hun Manet's voice to spread a message contrary to the truth.
incidents.notes: FreeLibrary reprint of the same Khmer Times article is dated 14 Nov 2025 (likely print date); Khmer Times online/Telegram and the AI Forum Cambodia newsletter cite 13 Nov 2025, which is used here.

incidents.title: Man arrested for using AI-generated fake news and images to solicit charitable donations
incidents.summary: A Siem Reap man allegedly used AI to create fake news and AI-produced images of orphans, and fabricated stories including fundraising for military heroes at the Cambodia-Thailand border and a grieving widow unable to afford a coffin, to solicit donations via five Facebook accounts with QR codes.
incidents.notes: 8 July is the arrest date stated by the Anti-Technology Crime Department; the fabricated posts themselves are undated, so onset is approximate. First published report found is 10 July 2025. Single-outlet account (Phnom Penh Post, reprinted in full by The Free Library).

incidents.title: AI-enabled impersonation scam calls from Laos target Spain; 3 million calls over nine months
incidents.summary: A Chinese criminal organisation used AI and phone spoofing to impersonate police and authorities, making three million scam calls from Laos to Spain over nine months; victims were deceived into transferring funds.
incidents.source_title: OECD AI Incidents and Hazards Monitor, 10 Jul 2026
incidents.notes: Date is the AIM entry date; the underlying press article was not retrievable from the AIM page in this sweep. The nine-month call window implies activity from about October 2025. No Lao official response specifically to the Spain case was found; the linked responses are the Lao government's 2026 crackdown on the same scam-centre phenomenon.

incidents.title: ChatGPT used by forced labourers in KK Park scam compound to impersonate Americans in crypto investment scams
incidents.summary: Trafficked workers held at KK Park, Myawaddy, on the Myanmar-Thai border were forced to use ChatGPT to craft messages impersonating Americans and trick US victims, including real estate agents, into bogus cryptocurrency investments (pig-butchering scams); other workers used it for romance scams.
incidents.notes: Reuters states it could not independently verify the full details of the survivor's account. Date is publication date; ChatGPT use predates it (survivor left KK Park in Apr 2025; other workers report use from 2022). Text impersonation via ChatGPT, not a video or voice deepfake; themed general-ai.

incidents.title: AI-generated fake news misusing Brunei Darussalam Central Bank name and logo
incidents.summary: AI-generated fake news misusing the name and logo of the Brunei Darussalam Central Bank circulated on social media, using clickbait headlines to harvest personal or financial information, promote unlicensed financial products and services, and trick victims into installing malicious apps.
incidents.notes: BDCB's own site lists the press release 'Beware and Stay Alert of Fake News Generated By Artificial Intelligence (AI)' dated 14 June 2024; the RTB text confirms the warning followed recent AI-generated fake news misusing BDCB's name and logo. Exact first circulation date of the fake news is unknown, hence onset approximate.

incidents.title: Deepfake videos impersonating Royal Brunei Police Force officers promote 'Real Money Magic' investment scam
incidents.summary: Short AI-manipulated videos and audio impersonating Royal Brunei Police Force officers circulated on TikTok, Facebook and Instagram; several videos from a single TikTok account promoted a fraudulent investment scheme called 'Real Money Magic', falsely claiming it could solve financial problems with guaranteed quick profits.
incidents.source_title: Pasukan Polis Diraja Brunei (Royal Brunei Police Force), 13 Jul 2025
incidents.notes: AIID dates this incident 14 July 2025, apparently following the Borneo Bulletin report; the RBPF statement itself is dated Sunday 13 July 2025, the earliest public record found. The RBPF's Malay text renders the scheme name as 'nyata kemunculan wang ajaib'.

incidents.title: AI-generated fake article promoting 'BTC 800 Lurotix' crypto scheme misuses Brunei Darussalam Central Bank name
incidents.summary: An AI-generated fake article promoting a non-existent crypto-investment platform called 'BTC 800 Lurotix' circulated, misusing the Brunei Darussalam Central Bank's name; it claimed limited daily registrations, a verification call from a Bruneian account manager and a mandatory BND 250 deposit, framed as a way to bypass impending government blocks after a scandal involving RTB Perdana.
incidents.notes: Incident date is the date of BDCB's debunk post; the fake article circulated before that and its exact first appearance is unknown. Content details per the search-indexed summaries of the official BDCB and Waspada.bn Instagram posts; the posts themselves were not opened directly.

incidents.title: AI-generated fake video impersonating Brunei Darussalam Central Bank senior officials promotes investment scheme
incidents.summary: A fraudulent AI-manipulated video falsely claiming the Brunei Darussalam Central Bank promotes an investment scheme circulated; the video impersonated senior officials, and BDCB clarified it does not offer financial products or endorse schemes.
incidents.source_title: Brunei Darussalam Central Bank press release, 30 Jul 2026
incidents.notes: One search-indexed summary gives the Instagram post date as 29 July 2026; the post is listed as 30 July 2026 and the press release is cited as 30 Jul 2026, so 30 July is used. The press-release PDF could not be fetched (network error); content per BDCB's own publications page and its verified Instagram post.

incidents.title: AI-generated fake videos of Royal Brunei Police Force officers go viral on TikTok
incidents.summary: Viral AI-generated fake videos depicting Royal Brunei Police Force officers were uploaded via two TikTok accounts and widely viewed; police warned the videos were false and made with AI and cautioned against similar videos on Facebook, Instagram, WhatsApp and Telegram.
incidents.source_title: Pasukan Polis Diraja Brunei (Royal Brunei Police Force), 9 Oct 2026
incidents.notes: The 9 Oct 2026 RBPF statement does not specify what the videos promoted; the same-day RBPF Instagram warning frames such fake TikTok accounts using AI videos of police officers as scams offering money or assistance via WhatsApp, which supports the deepfake-fraud theme. Exact first upload date unknown, hence onset approximate.

incidents.title: Deepfake videos impersonating AKPS director-general falsely claim support for aid programmes
incidents.summary: Two viral TikTok videos showing a face and voice resembling AKPS director-general Datuk Seri Mohd Shuhaily Mohd Zain falsely expressed support for certain aid programmes. AKPS denied the videos' authenticity, warned the public and said legal action would be taken. Distinct from MY-I-06 (6 Aug 2025): that was a single video by TikTok user 'Hermano Kedutaan' about passport documentation issues, aimed at damaging the DG's reputation; this is two videos, four months later, with false aid-support claims.
incidents.notes: Distinct from MY-I-06: different date (7 Dec vs 6 Aug 2025), different claims (aid-programme support vs passport documentation), two videos vs one. Date is the Bernama report date, the earliest public record found.

incidents.title: AI deepfake videos impersonate director Lý Hải and his wife to promote unverified health products
incidents.summary: AI-generated videos and audio impersonating director Lý Hải and his wife promoted tonics, supplements and other unverified products; Lý Hải warned on 1 May 2026 that the fakes were sophisticated enough to deceive viewers, especially older people, into fraudulent purchases. He had previously warned about the same impersonation in June 2025.
incidents.notes: Date is Lý Hải's 1 May 2026 warning, the earliest public record found; the videos had been circulating before that. No financial-loss figure verified. No response row: the AIM summary's 'authorities have intervened in some cases' names no authority, date or action; the only verifiable intervention found (HCMC police summoning two people, 8 Jan 2026) concerns the separate Quyền Linh fake-arrest videos (AIM 2025-12-08-ef7a), not this incident.

incidents.title: Ring sold nearly 1,000 bank accounts and used facial-data forgery software to defeat bank biometric checks (Thanh Hóa)
incidents.summary: A ring bought, collected and resold nearly 1,000 bank accounts; it used software that hijacked the phone camera and injected the account holder's stored portrait photo or video into bank facial-biometric checks, so the accounts could be operated without the holder present. The accounts were used to pay for gambling, money laundering and illicit advertising.
incidents.notes: Date is the 26 Jun 2026 report; the bust is described only as recent, exact day not stated. METHOD CAVEAT: sources describe a camera-hijack tool injecting stored portrait photos (Vietstock: software builds a video from the holder's photos); they do not call the tool itself AI. The deepfake framing comes from OECD AIM 2026-11-03-d510 and the 4 Nov 2026 National Assembly debate, where a delegate cited this exact Thanh Hóa case while warning about deepfake biometric fraud. instruments.notes: Passed 4 Nov 2025. First tranche in force 30 Dec 2025; AI/intimate-image tranche in force 17 Aug 2026; remaining provisions to follow.

instruments.title: National Strategy for AI 2020-2045 (Stranas KA)
instruments.summary: National AI strategy covering ethics and policy; a presidential regulation on AI is meant to build on it.

instruments.title: Personal Data Protection Law (Law No. 27/2022)
instruments.summary: Indonesia's general data protection statute, one of the laws used to oversee AI in the absence of an AI-specific law.
instruments.notes: Enacted and in force 17 Oct 2022 (Pasal 76; LN 2022/196). Two-year conformity period under Pasal 74 ended 17 Oct 2024. Implementing regulation PP 33/2026 (see ID-P-06) takes effect 16 Jan 2027; dedicated supervisory agency not yet established as of Nov 2026.

instruments.title: Ministry Circular Letter No. 9/2023 on AI Ethics
instruments.summary: Sets ethical principles for AI, including inclusivity, security and transparency. Compliance is not mandatory.

instruments.title: Electronic Information and Transactions (ITE) Law, as amended (2024)
instruments.summary: Core law on electronic information, one of the existing laws to which penalties for AI misuse currently refer.

instruments.title: Draft Presidential Regulations on AI Ethics and the National AI Roadmap 2026–2029
instruments.issuer: Ministry of Communication and Digital Affairs
instruments.summary: Two draft Presidential Regulations prepared by Komdigi after public consultation 8–22 Aug 2025: one on AI ethics (three risk tiers, no sanctions of its own) and one on the National AI Roadmap 2026–2029 (10 focus sectors). Harmonisation completed Apr 2026; both drafts initialled by ministers and awaiting President Prabowo's signature as of 11 Nov 2026. No Perpres number issued. Minister told DPR 26 Jan 2026 that signature in 2026 was the priority.
instruments.next_milestone: Presidential signature of both Perpres
instruments.notes: Roadmap period is 2026–2029, not 2025–2030. A 30 Oct 2026 report said the drafts were 'now being signed'; as of 11 Nov 2026 they were still awaiting the President's signature and no Perpres number exists.

instruments.title: National Guidelines on AI Governance and Ethics
instruments.issuer: Ministry of Science, Technology and Innovation (MOSTI)
instruments.summary: Non-binding guidance encouraging developers and deployers to adopt responsible AI practices voluntarily.

instruments.title: National AI Office (NAIO) launched
instruments.summary: Agency set up to accelerate adoption and shape AI policy and governance; widely seen as the lead on AI regulation.
instruments.notes: NAIO's own site gives an earlier establishment date (28 August); the launch is dated 12 December 2024. Institutionalised as AI Malaysia Berhad, announced by PM Anwar Ibrahim 28 July 2026; AI Malaysia Berhad now leads national AI coordination.

instruments.title: Licensing of social media and messaging platforms (8 million+ users)
instruments.summary: Platforms with at least eight million users in Malaysia must hold an application service provider class licence. Reports say X fell below that threshold and was exempt.

instruments.title: Online Safety Act 2025 (Act 866)
instruments.summary: Passed by Parliament in December 2024, royal assent 6 May 2025, in force 1 Jan 2026 with age-verification duties and subsidiary regulations. The minister has used its instruments against deepfake scam ads.
instruments.notes: One law-firm note dates the passage to December 2025; the legislative timeline above indicates December 2024.

instruments.title: Proposed AI Governance Bill: public consultation paper
instruments.summary: Consultation paper for what would be Malaysia's first horizontal AI statute, covering AI across sectors. Submissions closed 31 July 2026 (317 submissions from 218 entities); draft Bill completed by Sep 2026. Digital Minister Gobind Singh Deo told the Dewan Rakyat 29 Oct 2026 the Bill will go to Cabinet and is targeted for tabling by early 2027 — the earlier 2026 tabling expectation has slipped. Bill text not yet published.
instruments.next_milestone: Bill tabled in Parliament (government target: early 2027)

instruments.title: Law on Digital Technology Industry (Law No. 71/2025/QH15)
instruments.summary: The first Vietnamese law to explicitly mention AI, treating it as a strategic technology. Some articles took effect 1 July 2025. Its AI provisions were later replaced by the Law on AI.

instruments.title: Law on Personal Data Protection
instruments.summary: Vietnam's first dedicated personal-data statute, effective 1 Jan 2026 alongside implementing Decree 356/2025/ND-CP.
instruments.notes: Law 91/2025/QH15 and Decree 356/2025/ND-CP repealed Decree 13/2023/ND-CP with effect from 1 Jan 2026.

instruments.title: Law on Artificial Intelligence (Law No. 134/2025/QH15)
instruments.summary: Passed 10 Dec 2025 (429 of 434 votes) and in effect 1 Mar 2026. A risk-based, standalone statute described as the first binding AI law in Southeast Asia. National security and defence uses are carved out.

instruments.title: Cybercrime Prevention Act of 2012 (RA 10175)
instruments.summary: General cybercrime statute. Authorities ordered the 2026 Grok takedown under it. It was not written for AI deepfakes.
instruments.notes: Year of enactment taken from general knowledge; confirm against the statute text.

instruments.title: Data Privacy Act of 2012 (RA 10173)
instruments.summary: Foundation of data protection law and one of the cornerstones of the current AI governance regime alongside the national AI strategy.
instruments.notes: Year of enactment taken from general knowledge; confirm against the statute text.

instruments.title: National AI Strategy Roadmap 1.0
instruments.summary: First roadmap, focused on industrial competitiveness.

instruments.title: National AI Strategy Roadmap 2.0
instruments.summary: Updated roadmap adopted after the rapid emergence of generative AI.
instruments.source_title: DTI: DTI launches National AI Strategy Roadmap 2.0 and Center for AI Research
instruments.notes: Exact month verified (see backlog). DTI is reported to now label NAISR 2.0 an archived reference following NAIS-PH — confirm against a DTI source before changing status from in_force.

instruments.title: National AI Strategy for the Philippines (NAIS-PH)
instruments.issuer: Department of Science and Technology; approved by the Office of the President
instruments.summary: Presidential strategy approved by President Marcos Jr., described as the cornerstone of the current regime. Approved by President Ferdinand Marcos Jr. at a sectoral meeting on 20 May 2025; five pillars (infrastructure, workforce, innovation, ethics/policy, deployment), phased 2024–2028.
instruments.source_title: OpenGov Asia: The Philippines: President Approves Comprehensive AI Roadmap

instruments.title: COMELEC Resolution No. 11064: AI and social media in election campaigns
instruments.summary: Regulates AI and social media in digital campaigns for the May 2025 elections: requires disclosure of AI use in campaign material and penalises misuse for disinformation.
instruments.notes: Written for the 2025 elections; applicability to later polls to confirm.

instruments.title: House Bill 10567: Deepfake Accountability and Transparency Act
instruments.summary: Would regulate AI-generated deepfakes with disclosure requirements. Pending in committee; reported as under review as of September 2026.
instruments.next_milestone: Refile/substitute bill (HB 6314 or HB 7584) progress in the 20th Congress
instruments.notes: Pending in the Committee on Information and Communications Technology in the 19th Congress; no committee report or floor vote found. The 19th Congress ended 30 June 2025, so the bill lapsed; no refile under HB 10567 found in the 20th Congress. Successor deepfake work: HB 6314 (Fake News and Digital Disinformation Act) and HB 7584 (filed 3 Feb 2026, pending ICT since 9 Feb 2026).

instruments.title: Thailand National AI Strategy and Action Plan (2022-2027)
instruments.issuer: Cabinet of Thailand; Ministry of Digital Economy and Society
instruments.summary: Five-pillar plan covering ethical, legal and regulatory readiness, infrastructure, skills, research and sector adoption. A Prime Minister-chaired national AI committee was set up in August 2022.
instruments.source_title: Tilleke & Gibbins, 'Comprehensive Policy: Thailand's AI Governance Framework'

instruments.title: Digital Thailand AI Ethics Guideline (2022)
instruments.issuer: Digital Thailand (Ministry of Digital Economy and Society)
instruments.summary: Non-binding national guideline setting out six ethical principles for regulators, developers, providers and users of AI.
instruments.notes: Sources give 1 March 2022 and 22 March 2022 for different guideline entries, so year precision is used. The issuer is named at ministry level only.

instruments.title: Emergency Decree on Prevention and Suppression of Technological Crimes B.E. 2566 (2023), as amended in April 2025
instruments.summary: The April 2025 amendment, published in the Government Gazette on 12 April, set up a Center for Prevention and Suppression of Technology Crimes that can notify financial institutions of names and wallet addresses linked to technology crime. The final text dropped an earlier proposal to widen the definition to cover forged identity and biometrics.
instruments.notes: The original decree dates from 2023; this entry records the 2025 amendment. Law-firm bulletin; the Gazette text was not opened.

instruments.title: Notification of the Electronic Transactions Commission on Measures to Prevent Technological Crimes for Social Media Service Providers
instruments.summary: Issued under the amended Emergency Decree and in effect from 5 July 2025, it sets duties for social media platforms aimed at online fraud and technology-related crime.
instruments.notes: Law-firm bulletin; the notification text was not opened. Its specific duties are not summarised here.

instruments.title: National Cyber Security Agency AI security guidelines
instruments.summary: Recommendations for protecting AI systems from cyber threats, aligned with ISO/IEC 42001:2023 and the NIST AI risk framework.
instruments.source_title: Tilleke & Gibbins, Thailand's AI governance framework
instruments.notes: Month precision from a law-firm summary.

instruments.title: Draft Act on Artificial Intelligence (ETDA public hearing)
instruments.summary: New draft released for a public hearing of about 30 days. It would apply to AI development or deployment affecting people in Thailand, even from abroad; high-risk AI would be designated by royal decree; it adds a regulatory sandbox. An earlier set of draft principles had a hearing in May and June 2025.
instruments.source_title: Tilleke & Gibbins, 'Thailand releases new draft AI Act'
instruments.next_milestone: Outcome of the public hearing and a revised draft
instruments.notes: Law-firm summary; the draft text was not opened. Whether it names deepfakes was not checked.

instruments.title: Memorandum of agreement among the DOJ, PCO and DICT against disinformation and deepfakes
instruments.issuer: Department of Justice; Presidential Communications Office; Department of ICT
instruments.summary: Signed 13 April 2026 at DOJ Manila by PCO Acting Secretary Dave M. Gomez, DICT Secretary Henry R. Aguda and Acting DOJ Secretary Frederick A. Vida under 'Oplan Kontra Fake News'. The PCO leads public information, the DOJ legal enforcement, and the DICT technology, cybersecurity and monitoring. The Justice Secretary said the government will distinguish criminal disinformation from protected speech.
instruments.source_title: PCO/PIA: PCO, DICT, DOJ forge pact vs fake news, deepfakes
instruments.next_milestone: Primary release and any implementing guidelines
instruments.notes: Signing date verified as 13 Apr 2026 from the PIA republication of the PCO release. Exact PCO page URL not recovered; PIA URL used as the primary-government source.

instruments.title: Declaration on the Establishment of an ASEAN AI Safety Network (ASEAN AI SAFE)
instruments.summary: Leaders agreed to set up a regional network supporting the Digital Senior Officials' Meeting and the Working Group on AI Governance on AI safety. It operates on a voluntary and non-binding basis and acknowledges cross-border AI risks such as misinformation, fraud and content manipulation. Digital ministers adopted it in January 2026, and a Kuala Lumpur secretariat was announced.
instruments.notes: Names fraud and content manipulation generally, not deepfakes, so names_risk is no.

instruments.title: ASEAN Digital Economy Framework Agreement (DEFA)
instruments.summary: Signed in Manila on 14 November 2026 after negotiations that began in September 2023. Reported to cover digital trade, cross-border data flows, payments, cybersecurity and cooperation on AI, and described as the first legally binding standalone digital economy agreement in the region.
instruments.next_milestone: Entry into force and implementation plan (reports differ: first projects in early 2027, or 180 days after signing)
instruments.notes: Placed in the online-safety layer for its cybersecurity cooperation, though it is a broad digital-economy agreement. The signed text was not reviewed, so whether the AI provisions bind states or only commit them to cooperate is unconfirmed.

instruments.title: Protection from Online Falsehoods and Manipulation Act 2019
instruments.summary: General falsehoods law enabling authorities to act against deliberate online falsehoods, including through correction directions. Administered by IMDA through the POFMA Office. Can apply to deepfake falsehoods but does not name deepfakes or AI.
instruments.notes: Does not name deepfakes or AI; included as the general falsehoods regime applicable to deepfake falsehoods.

instruments.title: Online Criminal Harms Act 2023
instruments.summary: Enables directions, orders and information powers against online criminal activity, especially scams and malicious cyber activity. Directions/orders/information powers in force 1 Feb 2024; codes-of-practice provisions 24 Jun 2024. Police have said OCHA directions can be used against deepfake impersonation-scam content whether or not AI-generated.
instruments.source_title: MHA: Commencement of OCHA on 1 February 2024
instruments.notes: Does not name deepfakes in its text; deepfake-fraud theme reflects its use against deepfake impersonation scams.

instruments.title: Code of Practice for Online Safety – Social Media Services
instruments.summary: Issued under s.45L Broadcasting Act 1994 for designated social media services (Facebook, HardwareZone, Instagram, TikTok, X, YouTube). Requires measures to minimise exposure to harmful content, including sexual content, with enhanced protections for children. The instrument IMDA cited when engaging X over Grok misuse.
instruments.source_title: IMDA: Code of Practice for Online Safety – Social Media Services
instruments.notes: Does not name deepfakes or AI. A separate IMDA PDF of a general Code of Practice for Online Safety 2023 states 28 Jun 2023; 18 Jul 2023 is the Social Media Services version used here.

instruments.title: Government Regulation No. 33 of 2026 on the Implementation of Personal Data Protection
instruments.summary: Implementing regulation for the PDP Law (UU 27/2022): DPIA for automated decisions and new technology, Data Protection Officer duties, 3x24-hour breach notice, right to object to automated processing. Promulgated 16 July 2026 (State Gazette 2026 No. 88); takes effect 16 January 2027.
instruments.source_title: Recording Law: Indonesia PDP Law vs GDPR
instruments.notes: Sources differ by a day on promulgation (mid-July 2026); 16 July 2026 is used per State Gazette No. 88. Effective date 16 Jan 2027 per Pasal 225.

instruments.title: Malaysia National Artificial Intelligence Roadmap 2021-2025 (AI-RMAP)
instruments.issuer: Ministry of Science Technology and Innovation (MOSTI)
instruments.summary: Malaysia's first structured national AI framework: governance, R&D, infrastructure, talent, social adoption and innovation ecosystem, with seven responsible-AI principles and national use cases in five priority sectors. Superseded by the National AI Action Plan 2026-2030, launched 28 July 2026.
instruments.notes: Launch month March 2021 per UKM journal and US-ASEAN/KRI reports; Digital Policy Alert and AIPolicyTracker cite adoption on 1 Dec 2021 and note the exact date is not stated on official pages. Month precision used.

instruments.title: National AI Action Plan 2026-2030 (AI Nation 2030)
instruments.issuer: Ministry of Digital; AI Malaysia Berhad
instruments.summary: Five-year implementation blueprint for AI Nation 2030: 14 sectoral (Impact Engine) initiatives and 14 enabler initiatives under five enablers including Responsible Governance. Launched 28 July 2026 by PM Anwar Ibrahim alongside AI Malaysia Berhad (institutionalisation of NAIO) and the Malaysia AI Safety Institute. Successor to the AI Roadmap 2021-2025.
instruments.source_title: Ministry of Digital: AI Malaysia announcement

instruments.title: Artificial Intelligence Systems Cyber Security Framework (AISCF)
instruments.summary: Risk-based framework for securing AI systems across a seven-phase lifecycle (inception to retirement), applying secure-by-design and defence-in-depth across AI data, models, and infrastructure/applications. Launched by PM Anwar Ibrahim at the National Cyber Security Summit 2026, Putrajaya, with the National Cryptography Policy. Voluntary reference, not mandatory.
instruments.notes: Launch date 9 July 2026 from a taskforce contributor's record and summit coverage; NACSA's own PDF is undated in the excerpts checked. NACSA chief said pre-launch (Apr 2026) the guidelines would be a reference, not mandatory.

instruments.title: Risk Mitigation Code (RMC) under the Online Safety Act 2025
instruments.summary: Code under s.80 of the Online Safety Act 2025 (s.13 duties): licensed service providers must run harmful-content risk assessments, strengthen content governance, reporting and response, verify advertisers, and label manipulated content. Published 22 May 2026 after public consultation 12 Feb-31 Mar 2026; in effect 1 June 2026. Non-compliance can draw fines up to RM10 million.
instruments.source_title: Lexology: ONSA Child Protection Code and Risk Mitigation Code Published
instruments.notes: names_risk=yes because the Code expressly requires labelling of manipulated/AI-generated media. Enforcement from 1 June 2026 with a grace period for verification processes.

instruments.title: Child Protection Code (CPC) under the Online Safety Act 2025
instruments.summary: Code under s.80 of the Online Safety Act 2025 (s.18 duties): licensed service providers must protect child users, including age verification so only users 16+ may register, safety-by-design and age-appropriate defaults. Published 22 May 2026 after public consultation 12 Feb-31 Mar 2026; in effect 1 June 2026.
instruments.source_title: Lexology: ONSA Child Protection Code and Risk Mitigation Code Published

instruments.title: National Strategy on Research Development and Application of Artificial Intelligence through 2030 (Decision No. 127/QD-TTg)
instruments.summary: Vietnam's national AI strategy, promulgated by Prime Minister's Decision 127/QD-TTg. Targets top-4 in ASEAN and top-50 globally in AI research development and application by 2030, with three national big-data and high-performance computing centres, national AI innovation centres and open datasets. Directs work on a legal framework, infrastructure, talent and AI application; the Ministry of Science and Technology is the focal point for implementation. Non-binding strategy; the binding Law on AI followed in 2025.
instruments.notes: Signed by Deputy Prime Minister Vu Duc Dam on behalf of the Prime Minister. Takes effect from the date of signing. Superseded by Decision 1671/QĐ-TTg (National Strategy on Artificial Intelligence to 2030, vision to 2045), approved 28 Aug 2026 — see VN-P-07.

instruments.title: Decree No. 13/2023/ND-CP on Personal Data Protection
instruments.summary: Vietnam's first comprehensive personal data protection decree, effective 1 July 2023. Repealed with effect from 1 January 2026 by the Law on Personal Data Protection (No. 91/2025/QH15) and its implementing Decree No. 356/2025/ND-CP.
instruments.source_title: Medibase — Personal Data Protection in Vietnamese Digital

instruments.title: Decree No. 356/2025/ND-CP detailing implementation of the Law on Personal Data Protection
instruments.summary: Implementing decree for the Law on Personal Data Protection (No. 91/2025/QH15), issued 31 December 2025 and effective 1 January 2026. Expressly repealed Decree 13/2023/ND-CP.
instruments.notes: Also consider adding a note to VN-P-02 that Law 91/2025/QH15 repealed Decree 13 from 1 Jan 2026.

instruments.title: Personal Data Protection Act B.E. 2562 (2019)
instruments.issuer: National Legislative Assembly / Government of Thailand
instruments.summary: Thailand's general data-protection statute, modelled on the GDPR. Published in the Royal Gazette 27 May 2019; fully effective 1 June 2022 after repeated postponements. Thai PBS Verify cites it as prohibiting use of personal data such as face, name and voice without consent, making it one of the laws covering deepfakes.
instruments.notes: Gazette text not opened; PDPC enforcement record not checked.

instruments.title: Computer-Related Crime Act B.E. 2550 (2007) as amended by Act (No. 2) B.E. 2560 (2017)
instruments.summary: Core cybercrime statute used against false/distorted computer data. Section 14 covers dishonestly entering distorted or false computer data; Section 16 (as amended 2017) specifically covers doctored images of another person likely to cause reputational harm (up to 3 years / 200,000 baht). Thai PBS Verify lists it as the current law regulating deepfakes in Thailand.
instruments.notes: Year precision used for original enactment (2007); exact 2017 amendment publication date not verified. The Act does not name AI or deepfakes, so names_risk is no.

instruments.title: ASEAN Responsible AI Roadmap 2025-2030
instruments.summary: Adopted 5 March 2025 by all 10 ASEAN states. Gives policymakers customized, step-by-step guidance to operationalise responsible AI in an integrated and interoperable way, across four pillars: internal governance; skills and knowledge; risk mitigation and monitoring; stakeholder coordination and regional cooperation. Non-binding.
instruments.next_milestone: Implementation progress check
instruments.notes: Distinct from ASEAN-P-05 (AI Safety Network declaration). The ASEAN book page itself carries no date; the 5 Mar 2025 adoption date comes from Digital Policy Alert and Drew & Napier.

instruments.title: ASEAN Leaders' Declaration on AI-Powered MSME Growth
instruments.summary: Adopted 15 November 2026 in Manila. Sets a coordinated regional vision for AI adoption by MSMEs, with voluntary AI governance in line with national laws, lawful and ethical AI use, transparency, accountability, cybersecurity, data governance, human oversight, personal data protection for MSMEs and IP respect. Guided by the 2024 AI Guide, the Expanded GenAI Guide and the Responsible AI Roadmap. Philippines, as lead proponent, to report on the AI-Powered MSME Growth Action Plan.
instruments.next_milestone: Philippines' progress report on the Action Plan
instruments.notes: Outcome of the ASEAN AI Summit on AI-Powered MSME Growth, held virtually 6 October 2026 (not Cebu, September, as originally framed). The summit was announced at the 48th ASEAN Summit in Cebu, 5-8 May 2026.

instruments.title: Japan-ASEAN AI Safety and Security Partnership
instruments.issuer: Japan and ASEAN Member States (29th ASEAN-Japan Summit)
instruments.summary: Launched by Japan at the 29th ASEAN-Japan Summit in Manila. Voluntary, non-binding cooperation on AI safety, security, governance and assurance, focused on sharing best practices and information and capacity-building, in coordination with the ASEAN Working Group on AI Governance and the ASEAN AI Safety Network. Covers model testing, technical expertise and government evaluation capability, against risks including cybersecurity threats and loss of human control.
instruments.next_milestone: Work programme / budget / timetable
instruments.notes: No budget, staffing or timetable published yet. Distinct from the Japan-ASEAN Co-creation Initiative for AI mentioned in the same summit.

instruments.title: Draft National Artificial Intelligence Strategy 2025–2030
instruments.summary: Six strategic priorities and 41 strategic measures to make Cambodia a skilful adopter of AI in the short term and a participant in the AI development market in the long term, covering human resources, data/infrastructure, AI for digital government, sectoral adoption, ethical and responsible AI, and collaboration/research/innovation.
instruments.next_milestone: Submit to the Digital Government Committee and National Digital Economy and Society Council for review and approval (MPTC workplan, April 2025)
instruments.notes: Public consultation ran to 20 June 2025; national workshop held 1 July 2025. Formal approval not verified by October 2026 (Digital Watch Observatory) and PM Hun Manet on 17 July 2026 still described adoption as forthcoming, so status stays draft.

instruments.title: Draft Law on Personal Data Protection
instruments.summary: Cambodia's first comprehensive personal data protection framework, GDPR-style: data-subject rights including human review of automated decisions, mandatory certified data protection officers, data protection impact assessments for high-risk processing, 72-hour breach notification, cross-border transfer controls, and fines up to 600 million riel (about USD 150,000) or 10% of annual turnover, with a two-year implementation period after promulgation.
instruments.next_milestone: Enactment (promulgation); two-year implementation period to follow
instruments.notes: Third draft issued 23 July 2025; consultative workshop held that day with about 200 participants. Still a draft at the MPTC validation workshop on 5 August 2026.

instruments.title: Law on Combating Technology-Enabled Scams
instruments.summary: Five chapters and 24 articles creating five new offences: technology-enabled fraud; organising or leading a scam centre; recruiting or training others to commit such fraud; maliciously collecting personal identification documents or information; and a specific form of money laundering. Penalties up to life imprisonment, fines up to 1 billion riel (about USD 250,000) and asset seizure. Promulgated by Royal Kram No. NS/RKM/0426/006; National Assembly passed 30 March 2026, Senate approved 3 April 2026, effective on promulgation.
instruments.notes: Title variants in secondary sources: 'Law on Combating Technology-Based Fraud' and 'Law on Anti-Technology Fraud'. AI is mentioned only in the minister's dissemination remarks (officials must understand new tactics 'including the use of AI'); the law text as summarised does not contain an AI-specific provision, so themes rest on technology-enabled fraud generally.

instruments.title: Law on Prevention and Combating Cyber Crime (No. 61/NA)
instruments.short_title: Law on Prevention and Combating Cyber Crime
instruments.issuer: National Assembly of the Lao PDR
instruments.summary: Criminalises cyber offences including unauthorised access to computer systems, unauthorised editing of content, photos, video and sound, causing loss through online social media, dissemination of pornography through computer systems, and computer data forgery; establishes LaoCERT as the national computer emergency response team.
instruments.source_title: Unofficial translation, National Assembly (via Ministry of Industry and Commerce)
instruments.notes: KPL (Oct 2026) says the original law was 'adopted in August 2015'; 15 July 2015 is the date on the law text and per Tilleke & Gibbins and the Council of Europe profile. Promulgated by presidential decree No. 135/PDT on 28 Aug 2015.

instruments.title: Law on Electronic Data Protection (No. 25/NA)
instruments.issuer: National Assembly of the Lao PDR
instruments.summary: Governs the collection, processing and protection of electronic data; classifies data as general or personal/specific, requires consent of the data owner for collection, use or disclosure of specific data, requires Data Administrator consent for cross-border transfer, and designates the Ministry of Technology and Communications as the responsible authority.
instruments.notes: Date and number agreed by Digital Watch, Tilleke & Gibbins/Multilaw, CaseGuard and JD Supra. An ASEAN ATRC meeting report (Oct 2024) refers to a 'Law on Electronic Data Protection (2020)', suggesting a possible amendment; not verified - see backlog.

instruments.title: Instruction on the Implementation of the Law on Electronic Data Protection (No. 2126/MTC)
instruments.short_title: Instruction on Implementation of the Law on Electronic Data Protection
instruments.summary: Implementing instruction for the Law on Electronic Data Protection (No. 25/NA, 2017).
instruments.source_title: Multilaw Data Protection Guide: Laos (Tilleke & Gibbins)
instruments.notes: Number and date from the Tilleke & Gibbins guide; a second source confirms the instruction's existence but not its date. The instruction text itself was not checked.

instruments.title: Law on Cybersecurity (No. 87/NA)
instruments.issuer: National Assembly of the Lao PDR
instruments.summary: Sets principles, regulations and standards for the management and monitoring of cybersecurity; the Ministry of Technology and Communications is the central coordinating authority; defines critical national information infrastructure, establishes a National Cybersecurity Operations System, and requires cybersecurity incident reporting.
instruments.source_title: Rajah & Tann Asia, Regional Round-Up: Lao PDR Q1 2026
instruments.notes: National Assembly reviewed the draft on 23 June 2025 (KPL); law dated 25 June 2025 and published in the Lao Official Gazette on 20 March 2026. One LNTV Facebook post (8 Oct 2026) lists a 'Draft Law on Cyber Security' among items for the October 2026 NA session; this appears to mislabel the anti-cybercrime amendment and is not treated as contradicting Gazette publication.

instruments.title: National Strategy on Artificial Intelligence 2026-2035 (draft)
instruments.summary: Draft ten-year AI strategy; the Cabinet agreed it in principle at the September government meeting (22-23 Sep 2026) and instructed the Ministry of Technology and Communications to revise it, with greater focus on infrastructure, databases and personnel; the strategy is to be guided by UNESCO's AI Ethics Readiness Assessment (RAM) findings.
instruments.source_title: Asia News Network / Vientiane Times, 24 Sep 2026
instruments.next_milestone: Revised draft to return to Cabinet; no adoption date stated
instruments.notes: Agreement in principle reported 24 Sep 2026, following the government meeting of 22-23 Sep. Full strategy text is not public; no KPL report of the Cabinet decision was located. Corroborated by Laotian Times (via The Laos Briefing) and US-ASEAN.

instruments.title: Law on Anti-Cybercrime (Amended) (draft)
instruments.summary: Revises the 2015 cybercrime law for social media, artificial intelligence, digital financial services and cloud computing; 10 parts and 62 articles (49 revised, 12 new); Part II defines 12 cybercrime types including cyber fraud, unauthorised manipulation of digital content, dissemination of pornographic material through cyber channels and cyber-enabled violence against women and children; provides for a National Committee for Anti-Cybercrime and a 24-hour emergency response centre.
instruments.next_milestone: National Assembly adoption
instruments.notes: Presented by the MTC minister to the 2nd Ordinary Session of the 10th National Assembly; deliberations ongoing at time of reporting, not yet adopted. KPL is the state news agency (primary source).

instruments.title: Cybersecurity Law No. 1/2025
instruments.summary: Enacted 1 Jan 2025 and brought into force 30 Jul 2025 by SAC Notification 113/2025. Licences (3-10 years) for cybersecurity services and for digital platforms with over 100,000 users in Myanmar; platforms must retain user data up to 3 years and disclose it on written request; VPN services require ministry approval (1-6 months' imprisonment / MMK 1-10m fine for unapproved provision); extraterritorial reach over Myanmar citizens abroad; penalties for cyber misuse, online theft/mischief and unapproved online gambling. No AI-specific provisions were found in the law text or in law-firm summaries.
instruments.notes: FLAG: SAC-enacted law, legitimacy contested. No AI provisions: full-text search of the Lincoln Legal English translation for 'artificial' returned nothing. Implementing rules/licensing procedures had not been issued as of Sep 2026 (Search-Risk).

instruments.title: Electronic Transactions Law (2004), as amended 15 February 2021
instruments.summary: 2021 amendment added Chapter 10 on protection of personal information, including a broad Section 27-C exception allowing government access to personal data for cybersecurity/cybercrime matters relating to stability, tranquillity and national security, and Section 38-C criminalising creating false/fake news online with intent to cause public panic (1-3 years' imprisonment or fine up to MMK 10m). Myanmar has no standalone data-protection statute; this is the closest data-protection provision.
instruments.notes: SAC amendment, legitimacy contested. Status in_force is inferred (no repeal found); the 2025 Cybersecurity Law overlaps but does not expressly repeal the ET Law. No AI-specific provisions.

instruments.title: National AI Strategy and National AI Policy (2025-2030) [draft]

instruments.short_title: EO 131 — AI Governance Framework and NAIC
instruments.summary: Adopts the AI Governance Framework for the Philippines as the national strategic guide for policy formulation, regulatory coordination, institutional development and capacity-building, built on four elements (ethics and principles; standards and assurance; risk-based policy toolkit; enabling resources). Creates the National Artificial Intelligence Council (NAIC), chaired by the Executive Secretary with the Secretary of Economy, Planning and Development as vice-chair, reporting directly to the President; the NAIC coordinates, facilitates and monitors implementation and reviews the framework at least every two years.

instruments.title: NOTICE TO THE PUBLIC: Use of Real Persons' Likenesses in AI-Generated Images
instruments.summary: The NPC states a person's face and likeness are personal information under the Data Privacy Act (RA 10173), and photos and videos may also be biometric information; generating AI media from a real person's face or likeness and posting or sharing it is processing of personal data, which needs a legitimate purpose and a lawful basis (consent is the most recognisable but not the only basis). Without a lawful basis it may be unauthorised processing under Sec. 25, with criminal, civil and administrative liability. A fabricated image or video is false personal data; under Sec. 16(e) the person depicted may demand blocking, removal or destruction and complain to the NPC, which may investigate and issue compliance or cease-and-desist orders. Satire, parody and journalistic uses are recognised but only to the minimum extent necessary; the notice applies equally to public officials, and complaints involving minors get utmost priority.
instruments.notes: New instrument, not an update to PH-P-02: the Data Privacy Act itself is unchanged; this is a distinct 11 Aug 2026 NPC interpretive notice under RA 10173 Secs 3(g), 12, 16(e) and 25. No circular number and no separate compliance date. Title and date verified on the NPC's own site.

instruments.title: Scams (Countermeasures) and Other Matters Act 2026 (Act No. 21 of 2026)
instruments.summary: Omnibus anti-scam law passed 9 September 2026 and assented 24 September 2026. Gives police account-disabling orders (up to 30 days, one extension), disclosure orders and service-limitation orders (up to 3 years), and raises penalties for designated online services to S$10 million for code-of-practice and implementation-directive breaches. Amends the Online Criminal Harms Act so an anti-scam direction may be given by the operation of a computer program where the program assesses that an offence has been or is likely to be committed, or that online activity is preparatory to or in furtherance of a scam or malicious cyber activity offence.

The Act names scam risk, not an AI risk — AI is the tool for issuing directions.

instruments.title: House Bill No. 10362: National AI Governance Act
instruments.summary: Comprehensive AI governance bill filed 29 July 2026 by Representatives Chel Diokno, Percival Cendaña, Dadah Kiram Ismula and Kaka Bag-ao. Would establish a national AI governance framework and an AI Bill of Rights (transparency, explanation, non-discrimination, human review, data protection, synthetic-media disclosure), require six months' notice, consultation and reskilling before high-impact systems displace workers, create a multi-stakeholder advisory council, and set penalties of six months to six years' imprisonment. Pending in the Committee on Information and Communications Technology since 3 August 2026.

instruments.next_milestone: Committee action in the House ICT Committee

instruments.title: Governance Framework on the Use of Human-Centered Augmented Intelligence in the Philippine Judiciary (A.M. No. 25-11-28-SC)
instruments.issuer: Supreme Court of the Philippines (En Banc)
instruments.summary: En Banc resolution adopting a governance framework for human-centered augmented intelligence in the judiciary. Applies to judges, court officials and employees, court users (including lawyers) and vendors supplying AI tools to the judiciary. AI must augment, not replace, human judgment: it may not be the sole, primary or determinative basis for any adjudicatory outcome, and all legal reasoning must be independently formed by the human decision-maker. Sets principles of human-centered use, human rights, fairness, transparency, accountability, human oversight, privacy and data protection, security and sustainability, and creates a permanent Committee on Human-Centered Augmented Intelligence. Implemented through OCA Circular No. 47-2026 (11 Mar 2026).
instruments.next_milestone: Committee on Human-Centered Augmented Intelligence guidance and tool approvals

instruments.summary: Guidance paper setting out the BSP’s minimum supervisory expectations for AI adoption by BSP-supervised financial institutions. Built around five principles — Sustainability, Transparency, Accountability, Responsibility and Security (STARS) — applied across the AI system lifecycle (plan, develop, validate, deploy, monitor) and extended to outsourced service providers under a shared-responsibility model. Voluntary and non-binding.

events.title: Grok image-generation misuse and regional responses
events.summary: Image-editing features on Grok, built into X, were used from late December 2025 to create non-consensual sexualised edits of real people, including minors. Governments across the region took different actions within about three weeks.

measures.title: Malaysia says data centres must comply with US AI chip rules
measures.summary: Malaysia said data centres must comply with the US rules, and is investigating the local unit of a Singapore-based cloud computing firm that faces a US probe into whether it was used to get around export controls. An investigation is not a finding of wrongdoing.

measures.title: Singapore engages US authorities on the new rule
measures.summary: Singapore defended its standing as a trusted business hub, and said it was engaging US authorities to review the details of the new measure.

measures.actor: US Bureau of Industry and Security
measures.title: Licences required for advanced AI chips to four ASEAN countries
measures.summary: An interim final rule, effective 19 November 2026, requires export licences for advanced chips and servers shipped to Malaysia, Singapore, Thailand and Indonesia (reports also name Brazil), as places with an "unacceptable risk of diversion". Existing data centres providing such services have 90 days to obtain authorisation, and there are global controls on computing access above 12 million aggregate TPP for designated entities, including Chinese companies.

measures.title: Fifth person charged in an AI server fraud case
measures.summary: Singapore charged a fifth person in relation to an AI server fraud case. Charges are allegations until a court decides.

measures.title: 200 MW of new data centre capacity allocated to four operators
measures.summary: Singapore provisionally allocated 50 MW each to Digital Realty, Equinix, Keppel Data Centres and ST Telemedia Global Data Centres, on Jurong Island, through its second Data Centre Call for Application, the main way new capacity is allocated. Criteria include a power usage effectiveness of 1.25 at full IT load. The agencies will review the need for another call in 18 to 24 months.

measures.title: Customs stop a US$13 million AI chip smuggling attempt
measures.summary: Malaysian customs foiled an attempt to smuggle AI chips worth about US$13 million. The exact date is still to be confirmed from the customs department's own statement.

measures.actor: Ministry of Investment Trade and Industry (MITI)
measures.title: Strategic Trade Permit for US-origin high-performance AI chips
measures.summary: A mandatory permit for the export, transshipment and transit of high-performance US-origin AI chips, with advance notification where misuse or diversion is suspected.

measures.actor: US Bureau of Industry and Security
measures.title: AI Diffusion Rule introduced (short-lived)
measures.summary: A rule introduced in January 2025 to control the spread of advanced AI chips worldwide. It proved short-lived, and data centre investment in Southeast Asia surged by July 2025.
